questions.title: Nonparametric profile-likelihood inference for a scalar mean
questions.description: Focused L3 known-theory rederivation evaluation. The target publication identity, theorem statement, proof, reference implementation, and outcomes are withheld from runtime. Let X_1,...,X_n be iid real random variables with mean theta_0 and variance sigma^2 in (0,infinity). For a candidate theta, define the nonparametric profile likelihood ratio R_n(theta) by maximizing the product of n p_i over nonnegative masses p_i subject to sum_i p_i=1 and sum_i p_i X_i=theta. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the finite-sample optimizer and likelihood-ratio statistic from constrained optimization rather than naming a standard method. Treat strict-interior, boundary, and outside-convex-hull cases separately; derive the admissible multiplier interval, uniqueness of its root, positivity and normalization of the weights, and the zero-at-the-sample-mean identity. Then give a reviewable asymptotic expansion at theta_0 and prove the chi-square-one limit from explicit stochastic orders, stating exactly where iid sampling, a finite positive variance, convex-hull feasibility, and any stronger moment condition you invoke are used. Explain inversion into an asymptotic confidence set and distinguish pointwise asymptotic calibration from finite-sample exactness. Audit sign conventions, factors of two, root domains, degenerate samples, boundary behavior, and numerical stopping claims. Do not substitute a parametric Gaussian likelihood, Student t statistic, bootstrap calibration, package output, simulation, or theorem naming for the derivation. The required model-authored artifact is est_scalar_mean_empirical_likelihood and must implement the exact frozen run_estimator(request) contract as R source using language=r, execution_profile=scientific_wasm, and only declared base/stats dependencies; it may not call an empirical-likelihood package or optimizer that directly returns the requested method. Exploratory R or Python may test identities and numerical cases. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses fresh iid finite-variance samples, seeds and designs fixed before outcomes, and at least 2000 independent replicates per design. It checks exact executable identity, likelihood-ratio calibration at the true mean, and central chi-square-one acceptance with reported Monte Carlo uncertainty. These finite experiments test the implementation and asymptotic approximation on the frozen designs only; they do not prove the theorem or establish finite-sample exactness. Source replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable. Every unresolved mathematical, executable, empirical, numerical, or scope gap must remain explicit.

request_fields.name: observations
request_fields.meaning: The ordered iid scalar observations X_1 through X_n.
request_fields.shape: One unnamed finite numeric vector of length 3 through 1024, with values in [-1e6,1e6] and at least two distinct values.
request_fields.indexing: Input order is retained only for the returned weights.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject logical, character, list, named, empty, too-short, too-long, nonfinite, below-domain, above-domain, or constant vectors rather than coercing, dropping, sorting, clipping, or imputing values.

request_fields.name: theta
request_fields.meaning: The finite scalar mean value at which the empirical likelihood ratio is evaluated.
request_fields.shape: One unnamed finite non-Boolean numeric scalar in [-1e6,1e6], strictly between min(observations) and max(observations).
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject logical, character, list, named, nonscalar, nonfinite, out-of-domain, convex-hull-boundary, or outside-convex-hull values rather than coercing, clipping, or silently returning an infinite statistic.

response_fields.name: n
response_fields.meaning: The exact number of supplied observations.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must not be logical or fractional.

response_fields.name: sample_mean
response_fields.meaning: The ordinary arithmetic mean of the supplied observations.

response_fields.name: lambda
response_fields.meaning: The unique scalar multiplier solving the empirical-likelihood mean constraint in the declared sign convention.
response_fields.shape: One finite non-Boolean scalar for which every denominator 1+lambda*(observations[i]-theta) is strictly positive.
response_fields.indexing: One multiplier shared by all observations.
response_fields.edge_cases: Return exactly zero up to floating-point arithmetic when theta equals sample_mean.
response_fields.normalization: The unique root of sum((observations-theta)/(1+lambda*(observations-theta)))=0 in its open admissible interval.

response_fields.name: weights
response_fields.meaning: The maximizing empirical probability masses in original observation order.
response_fields.shape: Exactly n finite strictly positive scalars summing to one.
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not sort, round, truncate, or return unnormalized multiplier weights.

response_fields.name: minus2_log_ratio
response_fields.meaning: The empirical minus-two-log profile likelihood ratio at theta relative to the unconstrained empirical distribution.
response_fields.edge_cases: Return zero up to floating-point arithmetic at theta=sample_mean and do not omit the factor two.

response_fields.name: asymptotic_p_value
response_fields.meaning: The upper-tail chi-square-one calibration of minus2_log_ratio.
response_fields.edge_cases: This is not a finite-sample exact p-value.

invariants.meaning: The request is a named R list containing exactly observations and theta, and the response is a named R list containing exactly the six declared fields. Missing, extra, malformed, coercible-only, nonfinite, constant-sample, boundary, or outside-convex-hull values are rejected.
Returned weights are strictly positive, sum to one, and their weighted observation mean equals theta within floating-point accuracy.
The returned multiplier satisfies its declared root equation and determines both the returned weights and minus-two-log ratio through the exact declared formulas.
Permuting observations permutes weights in the same way while preserving n, sample_mean, lambda, minus2_log_ratio, and asymptotic_p_value.
Adding one finite constant c to observations and theta adds c to sample_mean while preserving lambda, weights, minus2_log_ratio, and asymptotic_p_value.
For finite a>0, multiplying observations and theta by a multiplies sample_mean by a and divides lambda by a while preserving weights, minus2_log_ratio, and asymptotic_p_value.
At theta equal to the ordinary sample mean, lambda and minus2_log_ratio are zero, weights are uniform, and asymptotic_p_value is one up to floating-point arithmetic.
Repeated calls on the same valid request return the same values and do not mutate the request or its observation vector.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen design, the assessment independently generates iid samples at the declared true mean, invokes the exact accepted estimator once per replicate, and fixes distributions, sample sizes, seed, chi-square threshold, precision rule, and replicate count before revealing outcomes.

Across the frozen finite-variance designs, the true-mean minus-two-log ratio approaches chi-square-one behavior: its mean and central 95 percent acceptance agree with their targets within predeclared Monte Carlo and finite-sample tolerances.

The finite simulations diagnose implementation and approximation quality only; they do not prove the limit, establish finite-sample exactness, cover infinite-variance laws, or replace unresolved theoretical and numerical gaps.
